accepted.name: service_requests_enriched_location
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  complaint_description,
  source,
  status,
  SAFE_CAST(EXTRACT(DATE FROM created_date) AS DATE) AS created_date,
  created_date AS created_timestamp,
  last_update_date AS last_update_timestamp,
  status_change_date AS status_change_timestamp,
  close_date AS close_timestamp,
  incident_address,
  street_number,
  street_name,
  city,
  SAFE_CAST(incident_zip AS INT64) AS incident_zip,
  county,
  state_plane_x_coordinate,
  SAFE_CAST(state_plane_y_coordinate AS FLOAT64) AS state_plane_y_coordinate,
  SAFE_CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
  SAFE_CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) AS longitude,
  location,
  SAFE_CAST(council_district_code AS INT64) AS council_district_code,
  map_page,
  map_tile
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_311.311_service_requests`
grain: unique_key, one row per 311 service request
accepted.description: Cleaned/normalized 311 service requests with canonical timestamp/date fields, normalized council district and latitude/longitude as floats. Useful as a standard cleaned 311 events table for temporal or spatial analyses and for joining to other datasets by council district or lat/long. | Use for: Time-series counts of requests by day/week/month; Spatial clustering or mapping of requests using latitude/longitude; Counts by complaint_description, source, status, or council_district_code; Join to other spatial/district datasets via council_district_code or lat/long

accepted.name: bikeshare_stations_latest
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  name,
  status,
  address,
  alternate_name,
  city_asset_number,
  property_type,
  number_of_docks,
  power_type,
  footprint_length,
  footprint_width,
  notes,
  SAFE_CAST(council_district AS INT64) AS council_district,
  modified_date,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY modified_date DESC) AS modified_rank
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations`
grain: station_id, one row per station-version (rank indicates recency)
accepted.description: One row per bikeshare station preserving the latest metadata (by modified_date) and exposing a modification_rank so consumers can choose alternate ranks. Useful for analyses that need current station attributes or stable station identifiers for joins to trips. | Use for: Current station counts and capacities (filter modified_rank = 1); Station-level time series of metadata changes; Join latest station attributes to trips by station_id

accepted.name: bikeshare_trips_casted_stations
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  trip_id,
  subscriber_type,
  bike_id,
  bike_type,
  start_time AS start_timestamp,
  SAFE_CAST(EXTRACT(DATE FROM start_time) AS DATE) AS start_date,
  SAFE_CAST(start_station_id AS INT64) AS start_station_id,
  start_station_name,
  SAFE_CAST(end_station_id AS INT64) AS end_station_id,
  end_station_name,
  SAFE_CAST(duration_minutes AS INT64) AS duration_minutes
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
grain: trip_id, one row per bike trip
accepted.description: Normalized bikeshare trips with start and end station ids cast to INT64 when possible and canonical start_date/time fields. Preserves raw station name fields for safe joins. Useful as the canonical trips fact for aggregation and joins to stations. | Use for: Trip duration distributions by subscriber_type or bike_type; Station-to-station flow counts after joining to stations; Daily trip volume time series

accepted.name: trips_with_station_join
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.trip_id,
  t.subscriber_type,
  t.bike_id,
  t.bike_type,
  t.start_time AS start_timestamp,
  DATE(t.start_time) AS start_date,
  t.start_station_id,
  t.start_station_name,
  ss.name AS start_station_name_official,
  ss.address AS start_station_address,
  ss.council_district AS start_station_council_district,
  ss.number_of_docks AS start_station_number_of_docks,
  t.end_station_id,
  t.end_station_name,
  es.name AS end_station_name_official,
  es.address AS end_station_address,
  es.council_district AS end_station_council_district,
  es.number_of_docks AS end_station_number_of_docks,
  t.duration_minutes
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips` AS t
LEFT JOIN
  (
    SELECT * EXCEPT(modified_rank) FROM (
      SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY modified_date DESC) AS modified_rank
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations`
    ) WHERE modified_rank = 1
  ) AS ss
ON SAFE_CAST(t.start_station_id AS INT64) = ss.station_id
LEFT JOIN
  (
    SELECT * EXCEPT(modified_rank) FROM (
      SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY station_id ORDER BY modified_date DESC) AS modified_rank
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations`
    ) WHERE modified_rank = 1
  ) AS es
ON SAFE_CAST(t.end_station_id AS INT64) = es.station_id
grain: trip_id, one row per trip with station metadata columns
accepted.description: Trips joined to start and end station metadata (latest station record by modified_date). Preserves trip-level grain and station ids/names for both ends. Useful for origin-destination analyses and for attaching station attributes like council_district or number_of_docks to trips. | Use for: OD matrices weighted by duration or trip counts; Analysis of trips by station attributes (e.g., council district, dock counts); Mapping trips with station coordinates after joining to station metadata

accepted.name: crime_events_daily_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  SAFE_CAST(EXTRACT(DATE FROM timestamp) AS DATE) AS event_date,
  primary_type,
  SAFE_CAST(council_district_code AS INT64) AS council_district_code,
  COUNT(1) AS incidents_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_crime.crime`
GROUP BY
  event_date,
  primary_type,
  council_district_code
grain: event_date + primary_type + council_district_code, one row per day/type/district
accepted.description: Daily aggregated counts of crime incidents by primary_type and council district (when available). Produces one row per date + primary_type + council_district for quick temporal and district-level crime trend analyses. | Use for: Daily crime trends by type or district; Comparing incident counts across districts for a crime type; Time series forecasting of crime counts

accepted.name: incidents_sharded_union_all
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  descript,
  date,
  time,
  address,
  longitude,
  latitude,
  location,
  timestamp,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS shard
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_incidents.incidents_*`
grain: unique_key (per-shard), one row per incident record across shards
accepted.description: Union of incident shards (incidents_YYYY pattern). Useful to get a single incidents relation across available shards. Includes shard suffix for provenance so downstream queries can filter by shard if needed. | Use for: Aggregating incidents across years/shards; Shard-level provenance or quality checks; Joining incidents to other tables by date or lat/long

accepted.name: waste_daily_site_weights
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  report_date,
  dropoff_site,
  route_type,
  COUNT(1) AS loads_count,
  SUM(load_weight) AS total_load_weight,
  AVG(load_weight) AS avg_load_weight
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_waste.waste_and_diversion`
GROUP BY
  report_date,
  dropoff_site,
  route_type
grain: report_date + dropoff_site + route_type, one row per day-site-route
accepted.description: Daily aggregated waste load weights by dropoff_site and route_type. One row per report_date + dropoff_site + route_type with total and average weights. Useful for operational summaries and trend analysis. | Use for: Daily tonnage per dropoff site; Route-level load patterns and averages; Operational capacity and trend reporting

accepted.name: crime_events_with_location
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  address,
  SAFE_CAST(census_tract AS FLOAT64) AS census_tract,
  clearance_date,
  clearance_status,
  council_district_code,
  description,
  district,
  SAFE_CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
  SAFE_CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) AS longitude,
  location,
  location_description,
  primary_type,
  timestamp AS event_timestamp,
  SAFE_CAST(EXTRACT(DATE FROM timestamp) AS DATE) AS event_date,
  year,
  zipcode,
  x_coordinate,
  y_coordinate
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_crime.crime`
grain: unique_key, one row per crime event
accepted.description: Crime events preserving lat/long and formatted date/time fields for spatial-temporal analysis. Keeps primary_type, description, district and year for flexible grouping and joins. | Use for: Spatial joins to other datasets by lat/long; Temporal analyses by event_date or year; District-level crime summaries
